quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, you must leave a note. Include your name, phone number, and address. Attach it securely to the vehicle you hit.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Even over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving. This includes drugs for colds, hay fever, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while affected by any drug that impacts your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What does this sign warn about?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed. Protect your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in good weather.
Brake hard as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast in wet conditions causes your tires to lose contact with the road. Your car rides on top of the water, called hydroplaning. Slow down when driving in rain or wet conditions to prevent this.

questions.question: When passing a car, when is it safe to move back into your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move back.
When you look over your shoulder and see the car is behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is a safe gap between your car and the car you passed. When you can see both of its headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and cold showers do not speed up this process.

questions.question: Where is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight road with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians. You could cause a collision.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a right turn at this location. Making a right turn here would be unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas or brake pedal to help your car regain balance. Steer in the direction of the skid to gain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.
Wherever signs and pavement markings allow passing.
In a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and pavement markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections or where your view is blocked by a curve or hill. Always assume an oncoming vehicle is hidden. Only pass where signs and pavement markings permit it, and only if you have enough safe space.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: You should allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space when driving behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcyclist brakes or falls. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one taillight.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Disappear into blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Disappear into blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks or buses where cars disappear from view. They are also areas where cars are so close to the truck that the driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter of a mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at on-ramps and be ready for sudden changes in road conditions and traffic flow.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Try to deal with one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: This red and white sign means you should:

options.text: Stop and check for traffic from both directions before proceeding.
Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you wish to enter or cross.
Keep a steady speed and check for traffic from all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic on the road you wish to enter or cross.
questions.explanation: A yield sign tells you to slow down and be ready to stop if needed. Let any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian pass before you proceed. You do not have the right-of-way.

questions.question: If a driver sees pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should the driver do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and drive around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross at a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you proceed.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: When following a motorcycle, allow at least a three- to four-second following distance. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts both you and the motorcyclist at risk. If the motorcyclist falls, you need space to avoid hitting them. Falls are most likely on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges or railroad tracks.

questions.question: It is dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely because:

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
They brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts you and the motorcyclist at risk. If the motorcyclist makes a mistake, you need enough time and space to avoid a crash.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood. A higher BAC number means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: If a car is about to hit you from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, your body moves backward. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat and put your head on the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:

options.text: Slow down.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign means "Stop." Come to a complete stop. Check for traffic and pedestrians. Go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Tailgating another vehicle.
Not watching carefully for workers and equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep going at normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and proceed carefully. Slow down before entering the intersection.
